concepts.name: Electric Charge & Current
concepts.description: Definition of electric current as rate of flow of charge (I = Q/t), direction of conventional current vs electrons, and units (Ampere, Coulomb).

concepts.name: Electric Potential & Potential Difference
concepts.description: Work done in moving a unit positive charge between two points (V = W/Q), voltmeters, and electromotive force.

concepts.name: Ohm's Law & Electrical Resistance
concepts.description: Direct proportionality between potential difference and current at constant temperature (V = I*R), definition of Ohm (Ω).

concepts.name: Factors Affecting Resistance & Resistivity
concepts.description: Dependence of resistance on length, cross-sectional area, material resistivity (ρ), and temperature (R = ρ*l / A).

concepts.name: Resistors in Series Combination
concepts.description: Same current through all resistors, total potential difference splits (V = V1 + V2 + ...), equivalent resistance Rs = R1 + R2 + ...

concepts.name: Resistors in Parallel Combination
concepts.description: Same potential difference across branches, current splits (I = I1 + I2 + ...), equivalent resistance 1/Rp = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + ...

concepts.name: Heating Effect of Electric Current
concepts.description: Joule's Law of heating: H = I^2 * R * t, practical applications (electric iron, toaster, fuse wire safety).

concepts.name: Electric Power & Commercial Energy
concepts.description: Rate at which electrical energy is consumed (P = V*I = I^2*R = V^2/R), Watt, Kilowatt-hour (1 kWh = 3.6 x 10^6 J).
keyFormulas: P = V * I = I^2 * R = V^2 / R

misconceptions.name: Current Consumption Fallacy
misconceptions.description: Believing that electric current is 'used up' or lost as it flows through a circuit component.
misconceptions.remediation: Charges are neither created nor destroyed. The number of electrons entering a component per second equals the number leaving it. Only electrical potential energy is transformed.

misconceptions.name: Series Current Attenuation Fallacy
misconceptions.description: Assuming that current is strongest at the positive terminal and decreases after each consecutive series resistor.
misconceptions.remediation: In a single closed loop (series), there are no alternative paths for electrons. By conservation of charge, the current is identical at every single point in the loop.

misconceptions.name: Parallel Resistance Addition Fallacy
misconceptions.description: Thinking that adding more resistors in parallel increases overall circuit resistance because 'more resistors are present'.
misconceptions.remediation: Each parallel branch provides an additional pathway for electrons. Adding pathways increases total conductance and lowers overall equivalent resistance (1/Rp = 1/R1 + 1/R2).

misconceptions.name: Constant Current Source Fallacy
misconceptions.description: Believing that a chemical cell/battery always pumps out a fixed current regardless of the load connected.
misconceptions.remediation: A battery provides a fixed potential difference (voltage). The current drawn is determined strictly by the connected circuit resistance via Ohm's Law: I = V / R.

misconceptions.name: Power-Resistance Misconception
misconceptions.description: Assuming higher resistance always means greater power consumption without verifying if current or voltage is constant.
misconceptions.remediation: When connected in parallel to a constant voltage supply (e.g. household mains), P = V²/R, so smaller resistance draws higher current and consumes MORE power.
